newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan Dec c/a surplus seen down 23% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan Dec c/a surplus seen down 23% yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus for December is expected to show a year-on-year fall of about 23 percent, economists said on Thursday.

A Reuters poll of economists produced an average forecast for the surplus in the current account in December of 817.2 billion yen, compared with 1.07 trillion yen a year earlier. The forecasts ranged from 750 billion yen to 920.0 billion yen.
The December current account figures are due to be released at 8.50 a.m. on Monday, February 10 (2350 GMT Sunday).
The current account is Japan's broadest measure of merchandise and services trade.
Economists said the pace of the decline was likely to slow in the coming months, with Japan's trade surplus, a core of the current account surplus, expected to stop falling due to the weak yen.

Companies are expected to beef up their export drives in the fiscal year starting in April to make up for a possible drop in domestic demand resulting from an increase then in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent.
"The decline in the current account surplus in December could be a temporary phenomenon. The surplus may start rising soon," said an economist at a major research institute.
The services deficit, an item in the balance of payments, is expected to have widened in December from a year earlier on an increase in the number of Japanese travelling abroad.
